entry.title: Meta ads is now available in AWS Quick
entry.summary: AWS Quick now has a Meta ads AI connector. Meta advertisers can use natural language in Quick to create, manage, and analyze campaigns while staying connected to the Meta ad management network, and combine Meta ad data with first- and third-party sources to build dashboards, documents, slide decks, and automated workflows.

entry.title: New in AWS Quick: More capable flows, an updated web experience, and agents that work together
entry.summary: AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work. Today we're releasing updates that help your team get more done: build and run business-process flows in chat, triage your day in the updated web app, get more complete answers from multiple agents at once, and connect new data sources like Meta ads and Amplitude.

entry.title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill
entry.summary: Self-hosting LLMs on GPUs means paying to recompute the same context on every turn. Distributed KV caching with Amazon ElastiCache can cut inference cost by up to 40% and time to first token by up to 80%. This post walks through the distributed KV caching skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS, which evaluates and sets up the cache from your coding agent.

entry.title: Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers managed cluster extensions for observability and user management, bringing declarative, API- and console-driven configuration to the software running on Slurm cluster nodes. This post explains how the extensions work and follows a platform team through a quarter of running a shared Slurm cluster with them.

entry.title: Introducing Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Global Inference Gateway: One endpoint across Regions and clusters
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod introduces the Global Inference Gateway, one managed endpoint that routes inference requests across your HyperPod clusters in one Region or across Regions. It picks the best cluster, fails over automatically, and authenticates every request with SigV4 and IAM over AWS PrivateLink.

entry.title: How Standard Bank Group automates AI risk assessment for generative AI
entry.summary: Standard Bank Group automated the evidence behind its generative AI approval gates. Working with AWS Professional Services, the bank built an assessment in its own AWS account that scores each use case against international AI standards and its own policies using LLM-as-a-judge on Amazon Bedrock, giving risk committees consistent, traceable evidence.

entry.title: Announcing Amazon Textract Insights: Verifiable generative AI for documents
entry.summary: Announcing the general availability of Amazon Textract Insights, a new generative AI feature of Amazon Textract. Describe the fields you need in natural language, submit a document or a mixed packet, and receive structured results with a confidence score and page-level grounding for each value, with no model training required.

entry.title: Amazon SageMaker Inference: 2026 launches in review, part 2
entry.summary: This second installment reviews 13 more Amazon SageMaker AI inference launches from 2026, spanning configuration recommendations, fitting more models onto each GPU, serving models too large for one instance, cross-Region routing, and post-launch tuning, bringing the year's total to 26.

entry.title: Use Kimi Code CLI with models on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Kimi Code CLI v2.7.0 adds a native Amazon Bedrock provider, so you can connect the open source coding agent to models like Kimi K3.1 Pro using your standard AWS credential chain (named profiles or SSO) instead of a separate API key. This post shows how to configure the provider and send your first request.

entry.title: Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
entry.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments now supports AWS Marketplace, so agents can discover and buy x402-enabled products, APIs, data, and content and pay in USD on the developer's AWS bill, with no stablecoin wallets or API keys. This post walks through a research agent that finds a tool, pays per request through AWS Billing, and answers with sources.

entry.title: How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers
entry.summary: When hundreds of agents serve thousands of developers, governance cannot be an afterthought. The BMW Group shares the practices and patterns its R&D teams use to build, govern, and operate AI agents at enterprise scale without sacrificing speed, quality, or compliance.

entry.title: Run your whole selling business in AWS Quick
entry.summary: Most sellers do not need another AI product to learn. They need the tools and information they already use brought together, so they can see what is happening in their business and act on it.

entry.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI now monitors your generative AI inference endpoints by default and tells you when a change could improve performance or lower cost. It tracks latency, GPU utilization, and serving configuration, then sends a finding through AWS Health with a one-click path to benchmark alternatives in SageMaker Studio before you apply any change.

entry.title: Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews
entry.summary: For organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people, every interview presents the same challenge: How do you give candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills while gathering the evidence needed to make informed hiring decisions? Structured behavioral interviews offer a research-backed approach to this challenge. They use consistent, job-related questions and clear scoring criteria […]

entry.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness adds Strands harness defaults, built-in tools, and lifecycle hooks
entry.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness now runs on the open-source Strands harness, bringing a recommended model, task-oriented defaults, automatic prompt caching, proactive context management, and new built-in tools. It also adds lifecycle hooks so you can run deterministic allow or deny checks at defined points in the agent loop.

entry.title: Amazon Polly launches voice cloning: A unique voice for your brand
entry.summary: Voice cloning in Amazon Polly is now generally available. Give Amazon Polly a few minutes of recordings from a consenting speaker, and it builds a custom voice that reads new text in that speaker's voice. Cloned voices run on the Amazon Polly generative engine and support seven languages.

entry.title: Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach
entry.summary: As enterprises scale AI on Amazon Bedrock, token spend can grow even as per-token prices fall. This post walks through six composable optimization levers, shows how Accenture applied them across four client engagements, and recommends a sequence for cutting AI token spend on your own workloads.

entry.title: From learning to leaderboard: How Cisco upskilled 1,200 engineers in agentic AI with AWS AI League
entry.summary: Cisco and AWS used Cisco Transformation Fest and AWS AI League to turn hands-on AI learning into a culture of building. A Cisco engineer won the 2025 AWS AI League global title and 1,200 engineers competed in 2026. This post shares Cisco's journey, lessons from the 2026 winning agent built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and how to host your own league.

entry.title: Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: Cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI gives your application one invocation path across the endpoints and inference components you already run, in one or more AWS Regions and AWS accounts. The router prefers its own Region and shifts new requests to another destination only when the local one can't serve reliably.

entry.title: Protect agent tool calls with Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
entry.summary: Learn how Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway keep sensitive data out of the tools your AI agents call. Added as a gateway interceptor, Skyflow de-identifies data before any tool, model, or log sees it, and restores it for authorized callers, with no change to your agent code.

entry.title: PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1 is now on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
entry.summary: PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1, a reasoning model built for real-time complex dialog, is available today on AWS Marketplace and Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. Discover it, evaluate it on your own data, and deploy it to a secure SageMaker endpoint in your own AWS account.

entry.title: Introducing enhanced infrastructure observability in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers enhanced observability to help you diagnose GPU training issues faster. It brings together diagnostic and profiling capabilities for training workloads on both Amazon EKS and Slurm orchestrators, pinpointing issues across GPU, network, and host layers.

entry.title: Using NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning on Amazon EKS
entry.summary: Learn how to run two memory-bounded Kubernetes Pods on a single NVIDIA A10G GPU using open-source NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning on Amazon EKS. This walkthrough builds a custom Amazon Linux 2023 image, installs KAI Scheduler and the GPU Fractioning Operator, and validates per-Pod GPU-memory contracts with enforcement and metrics.

entry.title: Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) on SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization now supports Full Fine-Tuning (FFT). This post explores when FFT outperforms LoRA across key benchmarks, examines the spectral properties of model weight matrices behind the quality gap, shares practical hyperparameter tuning guidelines, and shows how to get started.

entry.title: Exa boosts embedding throughput by 50% to index billions of documents on AWS AI chips
entry.summary: Exa's neural search engine is backed by an in-house vector database, so the unit economics of embedding tens of billions of web documents drive the business. This post shares how Exa optimized embedding inference on AWS Neuron hardware (Inferentia2 and Trainium2) with custom NKI kernels, reaching a 47% gain in performance and cost per million documents.

entry.title: Introducing workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
entry.summary: Large training jobs can stall or compute wrong results even when every node looks healthy. Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now adds workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks that catch these failures sooner and raise the goodput of your training workloads.

entry.title: Introducing the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard
entry.summary: The Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard compares 70+ foundation models side by side on quality, speed, and cost, directly in SageMaker Studio. Learn what the leaderboard shows, how AWS benchmarks models, and how to go from a shortlist to a deployed model.

entry.title: How Airbnb uses cost per task to operate coding agents on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Airbnb runs evals on real engineering tasks and uses Amazon Bedrock observability to choose models for its coding agents and control production costs. This post shows how cost per task guides model selection, why production spending can differ from eval results, and how to monitor latency, manage quotas, and attribute spend.

entry.title: Design responsible AI controls for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
entry.summary: Learn how to make RAG chatbot answers traceable with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, pgvector, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, logging sources, scores, and guardrail traces in SQL.

entry.title: Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity

This post shows how to issue an IdP certificate with AWS Private CA, configure a credential provider to trust it, rotate the CA, and protect the certificate.

entry.title: How Salesforce is advancing global-scale model serving with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: Learn how Salesforce uses the cross-Region inference router in Amazon SageMaker AI to turn fragmented Regional capacity into reliable model serving. entry.summary: Social Department, an AI operating system for entertainment marketing, worked with TrackIt and AWS to build QuickSearch: single-action queries that surface shareable scenes, quotable lines, memeable frames, and trend-aligned moments across large video libraries, using TwelveLabs models on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon OpenSearch Serverless.

entry.title: Connect Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs in a hub-and-spoke network with centralized inspection

This post shows a tested pattern for connecting Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs and MCP servers in that model, with the VPC Lattice resource gateway in the network account so every hop crosses the firewall.

entry.summary: A recap of the inaugural AWS Quick User Group DC meetup, where data leaders explored getting enterprise data ready for AI agents. It covers what's new in AWS Quick, Financial Independence Group's AI analytics journey, and hands-on app and no-code flow building.

entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference now supports NVIDIA Dynamo for distributed inference, with multi-node and disaggregated serving, KV-aware routing, and automatic fault recovery. Serve large models across many nodes without building the orchestration layer yourself.

entry.title: Reducing token costs and latency in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore JSON workloads
entry.summary: As production agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore process multi-megabyte JSON payloads, token costs and latency climb. This post shares three composable strategies: offloading heavy artifacts to Amazon S3, on-demand result paging, and dictionary compaction. entry.title: Cut generative AI costs: Code for rules, models for judgment
entry.summary: The biggest cost lever in a generative AI system is whether you call a model at all. Learn how to decide whether each workflow step needs a model, and map each option to AWS: deterministic code, a constrained decision call, or a right-sized model on Amazon Bedrock.

entry.title: Govern and discover records with common metadata in AWS Agent Registry

This post follows an MCP record from schema definition through registration, enrichment, approval, and discovery, so teams govern and find resources with one shared set of facts.

entry.title: 从奥德修斯的归帆到AI时代的魔法：无所不能的我们，为何越来越“无家可归”？
entry.summary: 在西方文学的长河里，同一位古希腊英雄曾有过两次截然不同的命运转折。 在荷马史诗《奥德赛》中，奥德修斯历尽十年漂泊，拒绝了女神赐予的长生不老与永恒青春。他动用所有的智慧与隐忍，只为穿过惊涛骇浪，回到故乡伊萨卡，与妻儿团聚。 然而，到了中世纪诗人但丁的《神曲》中，这位拉丁名为“尤利西斯”的英雄却被彻底改写——他放弃了故乡与家庭的责任，在垂暮之年依然渴望探索未知的尽头，鼓动年迈的船员驶出直布罗陀海峡，最终在永不满足的探索欲中船毁人亡。 从“奥德修斯的归家”到“尤利西斯的远航”，恰恰隐喻了人类从古典走向现代的精神转向。 01 从文艺复兴的“魔法”到现代人的“无家可归” 学者吴功青在《魔化与除魔》及解读但丁《神曲》的文章中，敏锐地捕捉到了这一现代性困境的源头。 文艺复兴哲学家皮科·米兰多拉曾宣告，人没有固定的本性，人是“自己的塑造者”，甚至可以通过“自然魔法”认识并驾驭宇宙。现代世界正是建立在这样一种双重逻辑之上： 一方面是对自然的“除魔”，剥离万物的神圣与神秘，将其还原为冰冷的物理法则；另一方面则是对人的“魔化”，人将操控自然的权柄收归己有，站在了世界的中央。 然而，当人把自然的魔力全部祛除，自己又像掌握了终极魔法一样无限扩张欲望时，危机也随之而来。人虽然赢得了掌控世界的自由，却也切断了与传统的联结，失去了敬畏与精神家园，沦为了但丁笔下那个漂泊无依的尤利西斯——一个精神上“无家可归的现代人”。 今天，这种现代性困境正在人工智能的浪潮中迎来最新的演进。 当大语言模型与生成式AI普及，普通人只需通过自然语言下达指令，就能像昔日的程序员、设计师或学者一样生成代码、剪辑大片、撰写长文。AI赋予了每个人一根近似于“皮科魔法”的魔杖。 但这种突如其来的“无所不能”，却让我们陷入了比以往任何时候都更强烈的悬浮感与无家可归的焦虑。 02 为什么拥有了强大的造物能力，我们反而感到更加漂泊？ 首先，是工具理性狂奔下的“目标迷失”。 AI极大降低了创造的门槛，让人很容易陷入一种惯性：因为“能做”，所以不停地做；因为“高效”，所以不断开辟新的战场。我们像但丁笔下的尤利西斯一样，在无限的信息海域中盲目远航，手段极其强大，终极目的却一片空白。 在无数个被AI加速启动的项目背后，我们很少停下来问一句：我到底要回到哪里？我的“伊萨卡”究竟在何处？ 其次，是“体感”与“在场感”的剥离。 正如学者程乐松在《留白》中所警惕的“心智外包”，当代码是AI写的、文案是AI生成的、创意是AI拼凑的，人与作品之间便失去了传统工匠那种一锤一凿的“摩擦感”与肉身联结。 我们虽然拥有了惊人的产出，内心却无比清楚，这些光鲜的结果并非完全源自自身生命的积淀。这种跳过思考与打磨直接获取答案的捷径，带来的是虚假的掌控感与深层的空心化焦虑。 更现实的是，边界的消失催生了“无限内卷”。 当所有普通人都被AI武装到牙齿，“无所不能”便不再是优势，而成了新的及格线。人们失去了传统职业分工和技能壁垒所提供的稳定坐标，彻底脱离了固定的位置，不得不在无限的可能性中永远奔跑、永远对比、永远害怕被时代抛弃。 03 在AI的“魔法时代”，我们该如何为自己“安家”？ 面对AI时代的“魔法诱惑”，我们该如何为自己重新安家？答案或许就藏在古典智慧与现代哲思的交汇处——重新找回“奥德修斯的航向”，并为高速运转的生命留出恰当的“留白”。 第一，分清“能做什么”与“值得为什么而做”。 技术可以无限扩展我们能力的外延，却无法替我们决定什么是有意义的。在动用AI这根魔法棒之前，我们需要先在内心确立自己真正的“伊萨卡”——或许是一段真实的家庭关系，或许是内心真正热爱的某件具体小事，又或许是生活中亟待解决的一个真实痛点。 让技术服务于你的生活，而不是让你的生活沦为技术的试验场。 第二，在看重的事情上，保留一部分“亲手打磨”的笨拙。 不要把所有的思考与创作都交给AI一键生成。允许自己慢下来，去经历阅读和创作中那种“扞格不入”的卡顿、挣扎甚至犯错。只有通过自身真实的时间与精力投入，人与世界之间才能建立起扎实的情感锚点，那份令人不安的悬浮感才会随之消散。 第三，重新肯认人的“有限性”，警惕“效率反噬”。 很多人用AI提高了工作效率，结果却发现自己更累了——因为省下来的时间立刻被用来承接更多任务，陷入了无休止的自我压榨。 真正的“留白”，是AI帮你用两小时干完了过去四小时的活，而你把省下的那两小时还给生活：去散步、发呆、陪家人吃一顿饭，或者仅仅是安静地读一本“无用”的闲书。 写在最后 在AI时代，写多少行代码、码多少字已经不再是衡量个人价值的唯一标尺。把成就感重新锚定在机器无法替代的维度上吧——去提出一个源自真实困惑的好问题，去体察他人未曾言说的情绪需求，去为最终的选择承担起作为人的责任。 终有一天我们会明白，真正的自由，不是像尤利西斯那样在无边无际的欲望海域中永无止境地漂泊；而是像奥德修斯一样，看遍世间奇景、历尽千帆之后，依然认得回家的路，在有限而具体的日常里，安顿好自己那颗渴望家园的心。

entry.title: Semantic diffing of formal policies with anti-unification
entry.summary: A textual diff of two formal policies flags every cosmetic change and hides the one that alters behavior. entry.title: Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod

entry.summary: The UK Amazon Quick User Group's 2026 roundup: three quarterly meetups, 150+ attendees, and customer stories from Arriva, Carsa, and Propulse Lab on using agentic AI and Amazon Quick to turn data into faster decisions, higher satisfaction, and scalable growth.

entry.title: Building intent-driven UI testing with Amazon Nova Act
entry.summary: Epsilon's Agentic Platform team delivers UI testing as a managed, multi-tenant service built on Amazon Nova Act and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool. Tests are written in plain English and run on browsers managed by AWS, giving every product team resilient, intent-driven testing with zero per-team infrastructure overhead.

entry.title: Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro
entry.summary: Turn a PHP-to-Java migration from a one-time leap of faith into a measurable, repeatable process with Kiro. This post walks through a reusable engine: a mechanical discovery scanner and an eight-phase, parity-first workflow that treats the original PHP application as the specification and verifies the Java port with a parity harness.

entry.title: Lend and borrow resources across teams with AWS Batch’s quota management for SageMaker Training jobs
entry.summary: AWS Batch quota management is a new scheduling capability you can use to divide GPU capacity into quota shares per team or project, automatically lend idle capacity across shares, and use preemption to run your highest-priority SageMaker Training jobs first, all without manual coordination.

entry.title: How MoEngage turned over 400 APIs into agent tools with AgentCore Gateway
entry.summary: MoEngage turned roughly 400 private REST APIs across 7 AWS Regions into permission-scoped agent tools with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. No per-service MCP servers, no public endpoints, and no 400-tool context bloat. See how OpenAPI specs, Cedar policies, and managed Amazon VPC Lattice egress made it work.

entry.title: Accelerate agentic AI with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS
entry.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model that pairs reasoning and tool use with multimodal understanding. This post explores its architecture and use cases, then shows how to deploy it on Amazon EKS, EKS Auto Mode, and Amazon SageMaker HyperPod EKS with NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM.

entry.title: Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Stand up a governed, multi-account Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post walks through the architecture and an open-source reference blueprint: the operating model, control plane, per-Workstream cells, separate inference and tool gateways, and a CI/CD evaluation pipeline that gates each agent before production.

entry.title: Distributed training with Ray Train DLCs and EFA on EKS
entry.summary: The Ray Train Deep Learning Container ships the full CUDA-through-EFA stack, so you build no image. This post walks through a reproducible sample that fine-tunes Qwen2.5-1.5B with PyTorch FSDP across eight GPUs on two EFA-enabled g6.12xlarge instances on Amazon EKS, using the container exactly as published.

entry.title: Accelerating software delivery with agentic QA automation using Amazon Nova Act – Part 3
entry.summary: As QA test automation spreads across an organization, organizing tests and controlling who owns them becomes the real work. Part 3 of the QA Studio series on Amazon Nova Act adds applications that organize tests and report health metrics, plus team-based user management that controls who can see and change what.

entry.title: AWS named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service
entry.summary: AWS has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) for AWS Connect Customer. This recognition marks an important milestone for our team, and it reflects years of work pushing on what's possible in customer experience.

entry.title: Announcing SOCI-indexed images for faster SageMaker AI jobs
entry.summary: Seekable OCI (SOCI) indexing for Amazon SageMaker AI training and processing jobs takes full container image download off the critical path. SageMaker AI lazy-loads your image to start containers in seconds instead of minutes, with no changes to your job definition. See the benchmarks and how to adopt it.

entry.title: Fix evaluation bias to unlock better models on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Property Finder found that 96.8% of their vision-AI evaluation labels were inherited from the incumbent model, hiding its true accuracy. See how they built unbiased ground truth, applied evolutionary prompt optimization, and selected a more accurate, cost-effective model on Amazon Bedrock, cutting cost by 86% across 11 image-quality attributes.

entry.title: Exowatt beats frontier models on accuracy with SageMaker serverless model customization
entry.summary: In this post, we show how Exowatt used Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization to build a repeatable AI pipeline that produces task-specific fine-tuned models for two deployment targets, edge and cloud, achieving higher accuracy than frontier models at up to 49x lower cost.

entry.title: Fleet-wide computer vision lifecycle at the edge with SageMaker SDK v3
entry.summary: Fleet-wide computer vision needs a model per camera, not one model for the whole fleet. This post presents a working Amazon SageMaker SDK v3 reference architecture that trains, quality-gates, compiles per-camera models with SageMaker Neo, and versions thousands of them, with an AWS Step Functions layer pacing fleet-scale retraining within account quotas.

entry.title: Groundhog Day for AI agents: Prompt caching patterns for using OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Every time an agent takes a step, it re-reads its entire context before acting. Here is how prompt caching for OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock lets your agent remember, cutting input cost and latency without resending the same tools, instructions, and history every turn.

entry.title: Build agentic retrieval on a Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with CDK
entry.summary: Build enterprise agentic retrieval on a Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with the AWS CDK: an agent that routes across two knowledge bases, retrieves through the AgentCore Gateway, and returns grounded, cited answers, with seven layers of observability and both on-demand and continuous evaluation, all deployed as a single CDK application.
